title: Tax-Free Travelling Subsistence Allowances
text:
Tax Administration Jamaica 
Practice Note 

  Tax-Free Travelling & Subsistence 
Allowances 

This Practice Note is intended only as a general guide and will support users to understand the 
relevant  legislation  using  plain  English,  identifying  the  most  relevant  sections  and  using 
appropriate  examples.  This  guide  must  be  read  in  conjunction  with  the  Income  Tax  Act.  It 
contains the Authority’s interpretation of the law as it stood at the date of this publication along 
with any associated practices, procedures and instructions. 

Under Section 12 (2) of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 a Practice Note is binding on 
the Commissioner General and all officers of the Authority until it is revoked. However, taxpayers 
are reminded that the publication of a Practice Note does not affect their right of objection and 
appeal or their right of access to the Revenue Court on points concerning their own tax liability. 

Comments and suggestions for the improvement of issued Practice Notes and suggestions for 
future Practice Notes are always welcome. 

February 3, 2022 

Ainsley Powell 
Commissioner General

This  Practice  Note  is  intended  to  provide  guidance,  achieve  consistency  and  facilitate  ease  of 
administration with respect to the submission of application for approval of Tax-Free Travelling 
Allowance, Sections 12 & 13 and Regulations 8 and 9 of the Second Schedule Part 1 of the Income 
Tax (Employment) Regulations of the Income Tax Act of Jamaica. 

This Practice Note modifies previous publication dated December 9, 2021.

 Glossary of Terms  

The following list defines various terms used throughout this Practice Note. 

Allowance 

Allowance In-Lieu 

Assignment of Motor 
Vehicle 

Body corporate 

Casual Mileage 
allowance 

Commissioned/Variable 
Paid employees 
(including Sales Agents)  

Commuted Upkeep 
Allowance 

Co-owner  

Designated Travelling 
Officer 

An allowance is an amount paid by the employer to an employee to cover 
anticipated costs or as compensation for conditions of employment, and are 
paid regardless of whether the employee incurs an expense. 
An allowance paid to an employee who is eligible for motor car upkeep or 
commuted upkeep allowance but has no motor vehicle. 
When  an  employee,  who  is  a  travelling  officer,  does  not  own  a  motor 
vehicle, but is in possession of one and uses it to perform official duties free 
of  any  encumbrances,  the  registered  owner  must  give  consent  for  the 
employee to use the vehicle. The registered owner must sign a declaration 
(Form  A)  giving  his  permission  to  use  the  vehicle  and  to  declare  that  the 
vehicle  is  not  being  used  to  claim  motor  vehicle  upkeep  in  any  other 
organization. The travelling officer must also sign a (Form B) to affirm that 
the same vehicle is not being used to claim motor vehicle upkeep elsewhere. 

An entity, association, or group of persons legally incorporated. 

An  amount  paid  by  the  employer  to  an  employee  to  whom  neither  a 
motorcar upkeep allowance nor a commuted upkeep allowance has been 
granted  but  who  uses  his  own  means  of  transport  while  travelling  in  the 
performance  of  any  official  duties.  The  amount  paid  out  represents  the 
actual  distance  (kilometres)  travelled  by  the  employee  using  the  rate 
prescribed in this PN and authorized by the CG.  
For the purposes of this PN, this means an employee whose earnings from 
commission  or  variable  compensation  exceeds  their  gross  basic  pay. 
Commissioned or Variable Paid employees usually focus on direct selling to 
customers and or quota-based transactions. Commissioned or Variable Paid 
“employees”  (including  sales  agents)  can  also  be  considered  to  be  self-
employed.  These  individuals  pay  for  the  daily  operations  of  their  motor 
vehicle  (including  gas),  their  meals,  their  hotel  accommodation  and  any 
other  incidentals  relating  to  the  work  they  perform.  They  must  file  an 
income tax return each year. 
An allowance paid by the employer where it is expedient and desirable that 
the employee possess his own means of transport which will be used in the 
performance of official duties. The employee in receipt of this allowance is 
not a designated travelling officer. This is a contribution toward the upkeep 
and running expense of the motor vehicle and the employee should neither 
be out of pocket, nor should he derive financial benefits beyond his direct 
costs.   
A  person  that  shares  ownership  of  say,  a  motor  vehicle,  with  another 
person. 

Employees who are required to possess and maintain a motor vehicle for 
the efficient performance of their official duties and who will be eligible to

receive  a  monthly  motor  vehicle  upkeep  allowance  provided  that  they 
maintain the vehicle in a road worthy condition.  
As defined in Section 2 of the Income Tax Act and the Second Schedule, Part 
1, The Income Tax (Employments) Regulations, paragraph 2. 
As defined in the Second Schedule, Part 1, The Income Tax (Employments) 
Regulations paragraph 2, this means any person in receipt of emoluments. 
As defined in the Second Schedule, Part 1, The Income Tax (Employments) 
Regulations  paragraph  2,  this  means  any  person  paying  emoluments, 
whether on his own account or on behalf of another person. 
For this PN, this means that the motor vehicle pledged to be used by the 
designated travelling officer is not also being used by another person in any 
public or private sector organization to claim similar motor vehicle upkeep 
allowances. The same motor vehicle should also not be subject to deduction 
for  capital  allowance  and/or  revenue  expenses  against  the  income  of  a 
trade,  business,  profession  or  vocation  carried  out  by  the  co-owner.  In 
addition,  there  should  be  no  impediment  or  hindrance      preventing  the 
designated travelling officer from freely using the motor vehicle.  
Employees who are designated travelling officers or in receipt of commuted 
upkeep allowance may also be paid an allowance at the specified rate per 
kilometre, for travelling in relation to official duties. The amount paid out 
represents the actual distance (kilometres) travelled by the employee using 
the rate prescribed in this PN and authorized by the CG. 
For the purposes of this PN, a modified PN refers to where the substance of 
a previously published PN is being changed. For e.g., if a previous PN held 
that a principle applied to ‘A’ but not to ‘B’, and the new PN holds that it 
applies to both ‘A’ and ‘B’ the previous PN is modified because it corrects a 
published position. 
An allowance paid by the employer where it is necessary for the employee 
to  possess  his  own  means  of  transport  which  will  be  used  in  the 
performance of official duties. The employee in receipt of same must be a 
designated travelling officer. This is a contribution toward the upkeep and 
running expense of the motor vehicle and the employee should neither be 
out  of  pocket,  nor  should  he  derive  financial  benefits  beyond  his  direct 
costs. 

The person in whose name the motor vehicle is registered. 

An amount paid to a designated travelling officer who transports another 
employee  on  official  duties.  The  amount  paid  out  represents  the  actual 
distance (kilometres) travelled by the employee using the rate prescribed in 
this PN and authorized by the CG. 
As stated in Section 2 of the ITA "person" means any individual and also any 
body of persons. 
“Just and reasonable rate” means a rate that is not inadequate, excessive, 
or unreasonably discriminatory. The charge for the service must be in line 
with the services being rendered and the rates agreed on by the employer 
as part of the company’s employment policy.

Travelling Allowances 

In RAIS, this is a single application for an individual for approval of TFTA 

A payment an employer makes to an employee as a repayment for amounts 
spent  (such  as  gas,  accommodation  and  meals)  while  conducting  official 
duties Reimbursements made to employees are the exact compensation for 
actual  expenses  incurred.  Generally,  the  employee  completes  a  claim  or 
expense report detailing the amounts spent. 
An  allowance  paid  to  an  employee  traveling  on  official  business  to  cover 
accommodation, meals and other associated expenses. 
For the purposes of this PN this describes a situation where the new PN does 
nothing  more  than  restate  the  substance  and  situation  of  a  previously 
published PN. 
As defined in The Revenue Administration (Amendment) Act 2013  
includes a person who: 
(a) 

is  liable  to  pay  tax  pursuant  to  a  revenue  law  of  Jamaica 
whether or not –  

(i)  The person is resident of Jamaica; 
(ii)  The tax liability is in question; or 
(iii) In the event, any payment is waived or remitted or 

no amount is found to be payable; 

(b) 

is  of  relevance  to  a  treaty  partner  in  respect  of  an 
international tax agreement. 

Payments made to an employee who is required to travel on the job and use 
his own motor vehicle for official duties of the employer.  These allowances 
are paid to cover maintenance and upkeep of the motor vehicle, traveling 
expense incurred by  an employee without a motor vehicle, other incidental 
expenses 
in  relation  to  the  traveling  on  official  duties  such  as 
accommodation, meals etc.

TAJ 

TFTA

 Purpose 

Tax Administration Jamaica 

Tax-Free Travelling Allowance 

Updated Practice Note 

1.  The  purpose  of  this  document  is  to  provide  guidance  to  TAJ’s  staff  members,  other 
government departments/ministries and other public bodies, tax practitioners/preparers, 
professional  accounting  bodies,  and  the  general  public  on  the  interpretation  of  the 
provisions of Sections 12 & 13 of the ITA and Regulations 8 and 9 of the Second Schedule, 
Part  1  of  the  Income  Tax  (Employments)  Regulations;  specifically,  with  respect  to  the 
application and approval for payment of a tax- free travelling allowances. 

2.  This PN will also clarify how payment of commuted upkeep allowance, mileage allowance, 
casual mileage allowance, passenger mileage allowance, subsistence allowance, and other 
reimbursements in relation to travelling should be treated. 

 Objective 

This Practice Note aims: 

3.  To  provide  guidance  to  persons  affected  by  the  law  and  to  the  officers  of  TAJ.    In 
accordance with Section 12 of the Tax Administration Jamaica Act, 2013 the CG may issue 
Practice  Notes  setting  out  the  interpretation  and  procedures  for  the  application  of  the 
domestic tax laws. 

4.  To promote and achieve consistency in the administration of the Laws relating to domestic 
tax  and  to  streamline  the  processing  of  applications  for  approval  of  tax-  free  travelling 
allowance to improve efficiency and service to taxpayers. 

5.  To provide taxpayers with certainty regarding the approval process for Tax-Free Travelling 

Allowance in relation to their business operation.  

 Scope & Background 

6.  In administering the Law and procedures relating to the approval of TFTA this Practice Note 
sets out the interpretation and administrative rules of the CG in respect to Sections 12 & 

7 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

13 and Regulations 8 and 9 of the Second Schedule, Part 1 of the Income Tax (Employment) 
Regulations of the ITA which governs incomes exempt from tax, deductions allowed and 
tax reliefs approved by the CG respectively.  

7.  Section 12 of the ITA and Regulations 8 and 9 of the Second Schedule, Part 1 of the Income 
Tax  (Employment)  Regulations  provides  for  certain  allowances  to  be  paid  without  the 
imposition of income tax (exempt). 

8.  Section  13(1)  provides  that  for  the  purpose  of  ascertaining  the  chargeable  income  or 
statutory income of any person, there shall be deducted all disbursements and expenses 
wholly and exclusively incurred by such person in acquiring the income.  

9.  It  also  provides  the  taxpayer  with  information  on  TAJ’s  position  with  respect  to  the 
guidelines for submitting an application using an eServices account via TAJ Tax Portal.  

10. This PN serves to inform employers of their responsibilities in ensuring that any payment 
made to a designated travelling officer complies with the procedures set out in this PN. 

11. The request to pay a TFTA is an application for permission to compensate the employee 
for the use of his private motor vehicle in the performance of duties for and on behalf of 
the employer.  

 Need for a Policy Guideline & Interpretation 

12. This PN seeks to provide guidance and clarity on underlying issues currently being faced 
by stakeholders when determining if an employee meets the requirements to be paid a 
tax- free motor vehicle travelling allowances by its employer. 

13. There was an uncertainty amongst employers relating to a request for making a payment 
for a TFTA being first approved by TAJ before it can be paid over tax- free to the employee.  

14. There was uncertainty amongst employers if the purpose or reason for making a payment 

for a TFTA must be demonstrated for each category of workers.  

15. There was uncertainty amongst employers if the CG’s approval to make a payment for a 
TFTA was based solely on the position being held by the employee.  The PN will establish 
that the scope, purpose and frequency of travel must be explicitly stated when applying 
for approval to make such payments. 

16. To establish that the TFTA is an allowance to be used to assist employees in meeting the 
cost of maintenance and upkeep of their motor vehicle which is used for official duties. It 
is not to be used in any manner to facilitate tax avoidance.  

8 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

 Employers’ Obligations & Responsibilities 

17. Tax-free travelling allowance requests are made on behalf of employees who are travelling 
officers; including sales agents who also receive part of their emoluments in the form of 
commissions/variable pay and who, subject  to paragraph 94 of  this PN, are required to 
travel  on  the  job  and  use  their  own  motor  vehicle  for  official  duties  of  their  employer. 
Other  tax-  free  travelling  allowances  can  also  be  requested  by  the  employer  for  other 
payments to be made to an employee to carry out his official duties.  

18. A submission must be made by the employer for permission/approval by TAJ of a wear and 
tear allowance (i.e. TFTA) in respect of the motor vehicles used by employees to carry out 
their official duties or any other allowance made to employees in relation to their travelling 
in furtherance of their official duties. Approval must be granted before any payment of a 
TFTA is made to the employee. 

19. With the exception of circumstances mentioned in paragraphs 77 and 78, an application 
made for any increase in approved TFTA and/or mileage rates should also be supported by 
an increase in the employee's basic salary.  

20. In  making  an  application  for  a  payment  of  TFTA  the  employer  must  clearly  state  the 
proposed annual amount to be paid, in addition to the annual gross basic salary and all 
other taxable allowance paid to the employee. 

21. Where an employer provides a fully maintained motor vehicle for the business and private 

use of its employees, no TFTA will be allowed. 

22. As  outlined  in  this  PN,  an  employer  must  ensure  that  in  making  a  payment  for  motor 
vehicle travelling allowances and subsistence allowance they are guided by the following 
principles: 

(a)  For every employee to whom a motor vehicle allowance is payable for all journeys 
on official business the employer must be able to verify that the employee has a 
reliable, road worthy motor vehicle or access to one. 

(b) The motor vehicle must be properly registered, licensed and insured in accordance 
with The Road Traffic Act and Regulations of Jamaica. These documents must be 
made available for inspection by the employer at specified times agreed by each 
party. (see paragraphs 28 - 30)  

(c)  For every employee to whom a mileage allowance, casual mileage allowance and 
passenger mileage allowance is payable for all journeys on official business, the 
employer  must  request  that  the  employee  submit  some  form  of  verification 

9 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

showing the dates, time of departure and arrival, distance travelled as well as the 
reasons for travel.  

(d) If an employee is appointed to act for  a specified period  in a position to which 
travelling is attached, such employee is deemed to be the holder of the office of 
employment and consequently the allowances attached to post will apply to the 
employee. However, the employer must ensure that the employee, acting in the 
position, satisfies all the conditions in this PN and/or satisfies all the conditions 
which were in place when the TFTA was first granted to the previous holder of the 
post. (See Section XIX - XX) 

(e)  Any payment made to the employee in excess of the approved TFTA must be taxed 

at the appropriate rate of tax. 

(f)  The submission of all motor vehicle documents, the completed declaration forms 
(Forms A & B), when needed, and the driver’s information as stated in paragraph 
375  shall  comprise  the  requirements  for  payment  of  TFTA  to  all  eligible 
employees. 

23. The purpose of the approved TFTA paid by an employer to a designated travelling officer, 

is to ensure that:  

(a)  no employee is out of pocket as a result of travelling on official business; and 
(b) no employee derives any pecuniary benefit from travelling on duty; 

24. Every employer should ensure that any TFTA so approved by the CG must not be paid to 
the employee in respect of journeys between his place of residence and his principal place 
of work for the  purpose of attending the office. Therefore, reimbursement for ordinary 
journeys  between  home  and  principal  place  of  work  and  vice  versa  is  taxable  because 
these journeys are not regarded as business travel. 

25. In the event that the conditions for payment of a TFTA are not met, and payments were 
made to the employee without the relevant deductions, the employer and the employee 
are bounded by the provisions of the Income Tax Act and the Income Tax (Employment) 
Regulations.  Therefore,  the  income  tax  and  all  other  relevant  statutory  payments  not 
deducted will be recovered. (paragraphs 41, 49, 55 & 83) 

26. Where  the  employee  is  either  temporarily,  or  otherwise,  without  adequate  means  of 
transport  available  to  him/her  for  the  performance  of  his/her  duties  a  tax-  free  motor 
vehicle travelling allowance should not be paid to the employee in respect of such period. 

27. The employer must also examine the motor vehicle registration documents to ensure that 

the motor vehicle being assigned is not registered as a - 

10 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

(a)  Company Owned/Leased Motor Vehicle, except in the case of a lease/hire 

purchase agreement by the employee. 

(b) Government owned motor vehicle 
(c)  Commercial Motor Vehicle 
(d) Public Passenger Vehicle or 
(e)  Rental motor vehicle 

The use of the above mentioned motor vehicles are prohibited for the purposes of payment 
of a TFTA. 

28. The employer must ensure that copies of the following documents are retained by them 
as part their record and for verification purposes should a request be made by a TAJ officer. 

(a)  Employee’s valid Driver’s Licence. 
(b) Current Motor Vehicle Registration Certificate 
(c)  Current Motor Vehicle Certificate of Fitness 
(d) Current Motor Vehicle Insurance Certificate 
(e)  Finance Lease/Hire purchase agreement 
(f)  Completed Form A and Form B declarations 

29. The employer must verify the validity of the motor vehicle documents presented by the 
designated  travelling  officer  who  will  be  paid  a  TFTA.  Should  any  of  the  motor  vehicle 
documents as expressed in paragraph 28 becomes invalid during the month a TFTA is being 
paid the employer may proceed with the tax free payment for that month.   

30. If the documents are not validated (renewed) by the next month for payment of the TFTA 
the employer, if he so wishes, may make a payment for travelling allowances, however, 
such payments will be taxable until the employee remedies the situation. 

 Requirements for the processing of TFTA applications via RAIS 

31. For an application to be approved, an employer is required to provide the CG with clear 
details of the specific duties and responsibilities of the employee assigned to the position 
for which travelling approval is being sought. 

32. Applications  are  submitted  and  an  approval  is  granted  for  an  employee  occupying  the 

position.  

33. The CG’s position is that the category of worker and the employee occupying such category 
are very closely connected or related. As such, the approval will be attached to both the 

11 

 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

position  and  the  employee  occupying  the  position.    Notwithstanding  this,  where 
applicable, the approval will also be linked to the motor vehicle declared.  

34. The application approval process must focus on: 

(a)  The category/position and 
(b) the employee occupying the position  

35. Therefore, an application must be made for each employee occupying a travelling post on 
the understanding that each employee in a particular category meets the eligibility criteria 
laid out in this PN.  

36. The employer, upon making an application for approval of TFTA, must prove to the CG that 
such persons are using the vehicles to perform the  job. The employer at all times must 
provide full and complete information to facilitate the timely processing of the application. 
The employer should apply to the CG stating:  

  The  TRN  for  each  employee  on  whose  behalf  the  application  for  TFTA  is  being 

made.  

  The  name  of  the  employee  on  whose  behalf  the  application  for  TFTA  is  being 

made.  

  The employee’s position. 
  Address of base operation of the employee. (i.e. employee’s work location) 
  The  annual  gross  basic  salary  attached  to  the  position  (i.e.  excluding  proposed 

TFTA). 

  The  annual  amount  of  prerequisites,  allowances  and  benefits  attached  to  the 

position. 

  The proposed annual amount of tax- free travelling allowance to be paid. 
  The period of approval for which the TFTA request is being made. 
  The scope (areas travelled) and frequency of the travel. 
  The purpose of travel, duties and functions of the employee. 

The following documents should also be attached: 

  Copies of motor vehicle documentation and driver information. 
  Completed Form A and Form B declarations where an assignment of motor vehicle 

is done. 

  Copy  of  employment  contract  for  the  employee  on  whose  behalf  a  TFTA  is 
requested. (where there is a future increase in motor vehicle travelling allowance, 
supporting documentation must also be attached) 

37. An  enhancement  has  been  made  to  the  online  application  for  Tax  Free  Travelling 
Allowances. (see Appendix 1). Driver Information & Motor Vehicle Information are now 

12 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

mandatory when requesting approval for travelling allowance. Provision has been made 
for motor vehicle documents and the completed  Form A and Form B declarations to be 
uploaded,  via  an  attachment  during  the  application  process.  Applicants  are  therefore 
required to add records as usual and also submit vehicle information via an attachment(s). 
The following must be uploaded with the application: (see Appendix 2) 

(a)  Employee’s valid Driver’s Licence. 
(b) Current Motor Vehicle Registration Certificate 
(c)  Current Motor Vehicle Certificate of Fitness 
(d) Current Motor Vehicle Insurance Certificate 
(e)  Finance Lease/Hire purchase agreement 
(f)  Completed Form A and Form B declarations 

38. The employer or his representative must enter all the details of employee for whom the 
request is being made, (including the annual tax-free travelling allowance requested). This 
can  be  done  individually  or  as  a  bulk  upload  with  a  maximum  of  20  records.  The  bulk 
upload can be facilitated by selecting the ‘Excel Upload’ button and the template can be 
found on TAJ’s website under the section for “Forms”. 

39. Where  in  any  year the motor  vehicle  which  was  originally presented  by the  designated 
travelling  officer  in  order  to  gain  approval  was  changed  the  motor  vehicle  documents 
relating to the new vehicle must be presented to the employer and a new request made 
to TAJ for approval. This is necessary as the employer needs to ensure that the new motor 
vehicle is free and clear from encumbrances.  

 Company owned/leased motor vehicles  

40. Employees  to  whom  company  owned/leased  vehicles  are  assigned  on  a  full-time  basis 
should  not  be  paid  a  tax-  free  travelling  allowance.  Instead,  the  benefit  derived  by  the 
employee  from  the  use  of  such  vehicle  must  be  determined  using  the  information 
contained in Appendix B of the Second Schedule, Part 1 of the Income Tax (Employment) 
Regulations. The private use value of the benefit where a company owned motor vehicle 
is made available for the use by an employee is expressly provided for in the legislation 
and as such this provision takes precedence. 

41. If a travelling allowance is also paid under such circumstances, then such payment cannot 
be treated as tax free and will be taxable. Where it is discovered that the employer made 
such  payments as a tax-free emolument  steps will be  taken to recover  the tax and any 
other  relevant  statutory  deduction.  TAJ  will  take  the  necessary  actions  to  recover  the 

13 

 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

relevant statutory deductions due by the employee who received the benefit. In keeping 
with the Second Schedule, Part 1, The Income Tax (Employments) Regulations, paragraph 
36, TAJ will take the necessary actions to recover the amounts so due from the employee. 

42. The Second Schedule, Part 1 of the Income Tax (Employment) Regulations, Regulation 11, 
states  that  “where  by  reason  of  his  employment  a  motor  vehicle  is  provided  (without 
transfer  of  the  property  in  it)  for  the  use  of  an  employee  in  relation  to  his  office  or 
employment  and  the  motor  vehicle  is  available  in  any  year  for  the  private  use  of  the 
employee or members of his family or household, the value of the benefit accruing to the 
employee  shall,  for  the  purpose  of  ascertaining  the  tax  payable  in  relation  thereto,  be 
determined by the Commissioner in accordance with the Appendix.” 

 Declaration of Ownership of Motor vehicle 

A.  Motor vehicle not owned by Travelling Officer 
43. When a travelling officer does  not own a motor vehicle but is in possession of one and 
intends to use it to perform his official duties free of any encumbrances, approval must be 
sought from and granted by the employer for the employee to be eligible for the applicable 
travelling allowance. Such motor vehicle being used to claim the TFTA should not be the 
subject of any travelling allowance being paid by any private organization, public bodies, 
i.e. Ministries, Departments, Executive Agencies or other agency of Government, a local 
authority, a statutory body or authority or a Government company. (see paragraphs 54- 
55  

44. Where the motor vehicle is not owned by the employee, the employer should approve the 
request for the use of the said motor vehicle. The request to use the motor vehicle should 
be supported by:  

(a)  A signed declaration by the owner of the motor vehicle as shown in Form A, (see 

Appendix 3) and 

(b)  A signed declaration by the travelling officer as shown in Form B (see Appendix 4) 

THE DECLARATIONS MUST BE WITNESSED AND NOTARIZED BY A JUSTICE OF PEACE.  

45. The employer should ensure that the declarations are properly completed and must be 

forwarded to the CG along with the: 

(a)  Employee’s Drivers Licence 
(b) Current Motor Vehicle Registration Certificate 
(c)  Current Motor Vehicle Certificate of Fitness 

14 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

(d) Current Motor Vehicle Insurance Certificate 

46. The employer must examine all these documents to ensure that the employee for whom 
approval  is  sought  has  all  the  required  documents  to  operate  a  motor  vehicle  in 
accordance with the Road Traffic Act & Regulations of Jamaica. 

47. The use of the motor vehicle assigned to the employee by virtue of the Form A and Form 
B  declarations  must  be  renewed  annually.  As  such  an  application  made  under  such 
circumstances must be done annually. However, this facility must not be extended beyond 
three (3) continuous years, whether for one or more vehicle. 

48. Where  it  is  discovered  that  the  motor  vehicle  so  declared  as unencumbered  was  being 
used by the true owner to claim similar motor vehicle tax- free allowances or used in a 
trade,  business,  profession  or  vocation  for  which  capital  allowance  and  motor  vehicle 
expenses are being claimed against such income, the TFTA granted to the employee for 
whom such a request was made will be withdrawn with immediate effect. 

49. TAJ will notify the employer as soon as such a breach is discovered. Any amounts paid out 
as TFTA during the periods so identified will be subject to the deduction of all the relevant 
statutory  deductions  by  the  employee  who  received  the  benefit.  In  keeping  with  the 
Second Schedule, Part 1, The Income Tax (Employments) Regulations, paragraph 36, TAJ 
will take the necessary actions to recover the amounts so due from the employee. 

B.  Motor vehicle jointly owned by Travelling Officer 
50. Where the motor vehicle is jointly owned by the employee requiring the TFTA and 

another person, approval may be granted on condition that  

(a)  The employee has free and unencumbered use of the motor vehicle for the 

performance of his official duties. 

(b) Motor Vehicle being used to claim the TFTA should not be the subject of any 
travelling allowance being paid by any private organization, public bodies, i.e. 
Ministries, Departments, Executive Agencies or other agency of Government, a 
local authority, a statutory body or authority or a Government company.  

51. For motor vehicles jointly owned, the employee requiring the TFTA will be required to 

submit  

(a)  A signed declaration by the co-owner of the motor vehicle as shown on Form A, 

and 

(b)  A signed declaration by the employee requiring the TFTA as shown on Form B  

THE DECLARATIONS MUST BE WITNESSED AND NOTARIZED BY A JUSTICE OF PEACE.  

15 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

52. The use of the motor vehicle assigned to employee by virtue of the Form A and Form B 

declarations must be renewed annually. As such an application made under such 
circumstances must be done annually by the employer. However, this facility must not be 
extended beyond three (3) continuous years, whether for one or more vehicle. 

53. In the case of a motor vehicle which is jointly owned but primarily used by the employee 
requiring the TFTA, the three (3) year limit as mentioned in paragraph 52 will be waived 
once the CG is able to confirm such use.  

54. Where it is discovered that the motor vehicle so declared as unencumbered, was being 
used  by  the  co-owner  to  claim  similar  motor  vehicle  tax-  free  allowances,  or  used  in  a 
trade,  business,  profession  or  vocation  for  which  capital  allowance  and  motor  vehicle 
expenses are being claimed against such income, the TFTA granted to the employee for 
whom such a request was made will be withdrawn with immediate effect.  

55. TAJ will notify the employer as soon as such as a breach is discovered. Any amounts paid 
out as TFTA during the periods so identified will be subject to deduction of all the relevant 
statutory  deductions  by  the  employee  who  received  the  benefit.    In  keeping  with  the 
Second Schedule, Part 1, The Income Tax (Employments) Regulations, paragraph 36, TAJ 
will take the necessary actions to recover the amounts so due from the employee. 

Notwithstanding all the conditions stated above each case will be examined on its own 
merit. 

C.  Motor vehicle acquired through a Finance Lease/Hire purchase arrangement 

56. In the case of a motor vehicle which the employee requiring the TFTA acquires through a 
finance lease or hire-purchase agreement and the ownership of the vehicle is vested in the 
lessor, and will be transferred to the travelling officer on expiration of the lease or hire-
purchase agreement, such motor vehicle can be permitted to be used for the purposes of 
obtaining the applicable motor vehicle travelling allowance. 

57. In such instances, the Lease/Hire-purchase Agreement must also be submitted along with 
the required documents as per paragraph 37. On completion of the Lease/Hire-purchase 
arrangement the employee must submit to the employer the relevant documents showing 
that  ownership  has  been  transferred  to  him/her.  This  document  must  be  upload  when 
applying for the next TFTA on behalf of such employee. 

 Commuted Upkeep Allowance 

58. There may be circumstances where it may be expedient and desirable that an employee 
possess his/her own means of transport which can be used to carry out official company 

16 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

business. This individual is by no means a designated travelling officer therefore, he/she 
may be granted a contribution toward the upkeep and running expenses in the form of a 
commuted upkeep allowance as authorized by the CG. (See Appendix 5 & 5a)  

 Casual Mileage Allowance 

59. An employee, to whom neither a motor vehicle upkeep allowance nor a commuted upkeep 
allowance  has  been  granted,  but  on  occasions  will  be  required  to  use  his/her  personal 
motor vehicle to carry out official company duties, can be paid fully for the actual distance 
(kilometres) travelled at the rate prescribed for casual miles as authorized by the CG.  (See 
Appendix 5 & 5a)  

 Mileage Allowance 

60. An employee in receipt of a motor vehicle upkeep allowance may also be paid a mileage 
allowance at the specified rate per kilometre for travelling in relation to official duties. The 
mileage  allowance  to  be  approved  in  respect  of  the  office  held  by  each  category  of 
employee will be in accordance with the amount referred to in the approved Schedule. 
There are specific rules in relation to mileage allowance for certain categories of workers 
as noted in the approved guidelines seen in Appendix 5a.  

61. Employees who are required to work outside of normal work days and who use their motor 

vehicles can also be paid mileage for actual distance travelled to and from home. 

62. The claim for mileage must be from the point of departure, being residence or the official 

place of business, whichever is nearest to the employee’s destination. 

At the discretion of the employer, an employee driving a privately owned vehicle may start 
and terminate his field assignment at his home or principal place of business, provided that 
reimbursement for such mileage will be based on the amount approved by the CG as mileage 
allowance as referred to in Appendix 5 & 5a.  

17 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

 Other Allowances & Reimbursements in relation to Travelling 

A.  Mileage Allowance to employee receiving a fixed motor vehicle upkeep 

63. The CG has instructed that executives, senior and middle managers who are in receipt of 
an  approved  tax-free  fixed  motor  vehicle  upkeep  allowance  will  be  allowed  to  claim 
mileage at the specified rate per kilometre for travelling in relation to official duties. This 
will only be allowed where such employees have travelled in excess of 200 km in a calendar 
month. For e.g. the eligible employee who travels 300 km during a month should make a 
claim for 100 km. effective January 1, 2022  (see Appendix 5 & 5a). Therefore, employees 
falling within these categories will not be reimbursed for the first 200 Km travelled in any 
calendar month. 

B.  Passenger Mileage Allowance 

64. If an employee in receipt of a TFTA transports another employee in his own motor vehicle 
on a business journey, the employer may pay a tax-free passenger mileage allowance in 
accordance with the amount referred to in the approved Schedule (see Appendix 5 & 5a). 

C.  Subsistence Allowance 
65. Subsistence allowance may be paid to an employee who travels in excess of eighteen (18) 
kilometres away from his place of work (one-way) and is absent for a period of at least six 
(6) hours in the day. The purpose is to cover actual expenses incurred or a payment in lieu 
of actual expenditures such as short stay accommodation and meals.  

66. The amount is intended to act as a reimbursable expense and as a result would not be 
considered as a benefit and would not be taxed. Payments made to employees, that are 
termed  subsistence  allowances,  should  be  paid  at  a  rate  which  is  intended  to  only 
reimburse the employee for the actual expenditure incurred.  

67. The  CG  must  approve  the  payment  for  it  to  be  classified  as  tax-free.  The  employer  is 
required to make a submission to the CG for an approved amount that will ensure that the 
employee is not out of pocket while carrying out official duties.   

68. Where payments for accommodation and meals are provided and paid for by the employer 
before the employee engages in travelling on official duty the employee will not be eligible 
for the subsistence allowance. 

69. Given the nature of the work, the employee may be required to stay for short periods away 
from his place of residence. In such instances, the employer is allowed to pay an advance 
on the subsistence allowance on the understanding that the appropriate supporting bills 
are submitted.  Such advances should cover expenses such as short stay accommodation, 

18 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

meals, or any expense directly incurred by the employee in carrying out their official duties 
while they are away from their place of work. 

Subsistence in any other form not approved by the CG is taxable. 

D.  Reimbursements 
70. Other than the payment of a subsistence allowance, the employer may choose instead to 
reimburse the employee for any actual expenditures incurred in the furtherance of their 
official duties.  TAJ will allow the employer to make such reimbursements to the employee 
for any expenditures where, by reason of the duties of his employment, the employee is 
obliged to spend a part of a day or more away from his usual place of employment and 
provides  proof  of  such  expenditure  to  the  employer.  The  supporting  evidence  must  be 
kept as part to the employer’s records and presented if requested by a TAJ Officer. 

71. Where the actual expenditures incurred (e.g. meals, accommodation, parking ticket) by 
the employee to carry out his official duties exceeds the subsistence allowance approved 
by  the  CG,  the  employer  is  allowed  to  reimburse  the  actual  expenses  in  lieu  of  a 
subsistence  allowance,  on  presentation  of  bona  fide  bills  reflecting  reasonable  rates. 
Therefore, the employee will be able to recover the actual amount expended so as not to 
be out-of-pocket.  

72. However, please note, the employee cannot receive both a subsistence allowance and a 
reimbursement  which  will  cause  him  to  earn  a  monetary  advantage.  The  total  pay-out 
must be capped at the actual amount expended in keeping with reasonable rates agreed 
on by the employer.   

E.  Allowance In-Lieu 
73. An employee holding a post to which a motorcar upkeep or commuted upkeep allowance 
is attached but who has no motorcar may be eligible for an allowance at the prescribed 
rate. (e.g. “Commuted without motor vehicle”). An employee in receipt of this allowance 
will not be eligible for reimbursement of taxi fares or bus fares.  

 Provision of Fuel (Gas cards) 

74. The provision of fuel by way of gas cards or gas related payments or any other method by 
an  employer  to  or  on  behalf  of  its  employees  for  use  of  their  personal  motor  vehicles 
represents a taxable benefit (emolument) to the employees and should be taxed in full. 
Employers are therefore not permitted to treat the provision of fuel related benefits as a 
part of the employees’ tax- free travelling allowance. (The effective date of this document 

19 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

is not applicable to this paragraph since provision of fuel (Gas Cards) has always been a 
taxable benefit). 

75. In light of this fact, where it is found that an employer is providing the above-mentioned 
benefit and is not treating the value of the fuel related benefit as a taxable emolument the 
annual value of the fuel benefit will impact the final amount approved by the CG as a TFTA. 
Therefore, the CG, in exercising his discretion in determining the amount of income tax 
relief that can be approved in relation to any TFTA as mentioned in the PN, will reduce the 
approved value of the TFTA as allowed in accordance with the schedule of rates (Appendix 
5 & 5a), or reduce the lesser amount which was requested by the employer and approved 
by TAJ, by the annual value of this fuel related benefit.     

 How to apply for an increase in TFTA  

76. An employer can apply for an increase in TFTA whenever  
(i)  An employee has an increase in basic salary 
(ii)  The employee's circumstance requires a change in the category of travelling 
(iii) An employee changes to a higher job category 
(iv) TAJ announces an increase in the approved rates 

77. A  request  for  an  increase  in  TFTA  brought  on  by  a  need  to  change  the  category  of  an 

employee's approved TFTA, such as when  

(i)  an employee is moving from using a motor bike to a motor car in the performance 

of his duties, or  

(ii)  an employee is moving from commuted without motor vehicle to commuted with 

motor vehicle 

 the application for an increase will not be required to be accompanied by an increase in 
the employee's basic pay. (See paragraph 19)  

78. Any  employer  who  is  requesting  an  increase  in  TFTA  for  particular  employees  should 
provide the CG with the current information as circumstances and conditions could have 
changed  since  the  last  approval.  For  example,  a  promotion,  change  in  job  function  of 
employee who may now be entitled to say, approved TFTA for a senior manager from that 
of a middle manager. 

79. The current annual gross basic salary must be stated when there is a request for payment 
of  a  TFTA.  The  amount  declared  should  be  the  annual  gross  basic  salary,  plus  all  other 
taxable allowances, excluding the newly proposed TFTA.  

20 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

 Reduction in annual gross basic salary 

80. The employee’s annual gross basic salary plus all taxable allowances must not be reduced 

in order to make an application for payment of a TFTA.  

81. In instances where prior approval was granted by the CG for a TFTA and an increase in the 
amount is now requested the employer should not reduce the annual gross basic salary 
and  other  taxable  allowances  of  the  employee  to  facilitate  this  request.  Any  such 
application will be denied.  

82. Where a TFTA was approved  and  it is then discovered that an employee’s annual gross 
basic salary plus any other taxable allowance was reduced in order to apply for a TFTA the 
approval will be withdrawn with immediate effect. 

83. TAJ will notify the employer as soon as the breach is discovered. Any TFTA paid out during 
the  period of the  breach  will  be  recoverable and  TAJ  will  take the  necessary actions to 
recover  the  amounts  so  due,  which  will  then  be  subject  to  the  relevant  statutory 
deductions  by  the  employee  who  received  the  benefit.  In  keeping  with  the  Second 
Schedule, Part 1, The Income Tax (Employments) Regulations, paragraph 36, TAJ will take 
the necessary actions to recover the amounts so due from the employee. 

 Change in company name and ownership 

84. Where there is a change in ownership of the business and the employer is now operating 
under a new name and a new TRN any previous approval granted under the name of the 
previous employer is now invalid. 

85. A new application must be made by the current employer, even if the management and 
operational staff structure remains the same. That is, even if the company re-employs the 
same  staff  in  a  similar  capacity  and  the  annual  gross  basic  salary  and  all  taxable 
emoluments  remains  the  same,  the  previous  approval  cannot  be  applied  to  this 
employment.  

86. Where there is a change in ownership and the employer is now operating under a new 
name but has the same TRN any previous approval granted is still valid. However, this is 
only applicable if the following conditions remain in place: 

(a)  There  is  no  renegotiation  of  salaries  and  benefits.  Therefore,  there  can  be  no 
change in the annual gross basic salary and all other benefits, including the TFTA, 
previously approved. 

21 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

(b) The employees who were approved in the particular positions under the previous 

submission continue to occupy these posts.  

(c)  There  is  no  change  in  the  job  responsibilities  attached  to  the  particular position 

approved in the previous submission.  

87. Where the conditions under paragraph 86 (a –c) are not maintained, the employer must 

now submit a new application for approval.  

 Employees temporarily occupying a designated travelling 
position 

88. Where  the  employer  has  temporarily  placed  an  employee  in  a  designated  travelling 
position to facilitate another person proceeding on vacation leave, then the CG will allow 
the approved TFTA to be extended to the person now occupying the position. This will be 
allowed provided that the employee to the position satisfies all the conditions which were 
in place when the TFTA was first granted. 

89. In instances where the assigned employee to a specific category of work has temporarily 
vacated  the  position  as  a  result  of  leave  of  absence  or  assignment  to  another/higher 
position the employer must ensure that the new employee to the position satisfies all the 
conditions  which  were  in  place  when the  TFTA was  first  granted.  The  CG  will  allow the 
approved  TFTA  to  be  extended  to  the  person  now  occupying  the  position.  This  will  be 
allowed provided that the employee to the position satisfies all the conditions which were 
in place when the TFTA was first granted. 

90. For all other temporary displacements (e.g. study leave, extended leave of absence, etc.) 
the  employer  must  apply  for  approval  of  TFTA  for  the  employee  now  assigned  to  the 
position. As such, an application will be required in cases where: 

(a)  The new employee to the position was never previously approved by TAJ to be paid 

a TFTA 

(b) The conditions differ, e.g. salary earned is different, person is earning a commission, 
not registered to operate a motor vehicle in accordance with the Road Traffic Act & 
Regulations of Jamaica. 

(c)  The assignment becomes permanent. 

22 

 
 
 
 
 UPN-IT/TFTA-01-2022 

 Employees with approved TFTA now occupying higher & 
different positions  

91. Where an approval was granted within the calendar year for an employee in a previous 
category and this employee has now moved within the same calendar year into a higher 
or different position which still carries a travelling allowance: 

(a)  The employer must ensure that all conditions as laid out under paragraphs 36 – 
39, 44 & 51 are met before paying the individual a higher tax- free allowance.  
(b) The employer should apply the rates as prescribed in Appendix 5 & 5a of this PN. 

 Effective date of approval 

92. Generally,  where  applications  are  received  without  the  request  for  an  effective  date, 

approval is granted as follows: 

(a)  Where the application is received on or before the 15th of the month the approved 

effective date will be at the 1st day of that month. 

(b) Where applications are received after the 15th of the month approved effective 

date will be effective the 1st day of the following month. 

Where TAJ has requested additional information and documents the effective date may 
be impacted and the CG will therefore make a determination. 

93. In instances where applications are received requesting a retroactive effective date the CG 

may grant an approval. However, the employer must ensure that  

(a)  The  CG  is  provided  with  a  reasonable  cause  as  to  why  the  submission  of  the 

application is late thus rendering the need for a retroactive date; and 

(b)  Proper justification must be provided to validate the eligibility of the employee on 

whose behalf the request is now made. 

Notwithstanding,  due  diligence  must  be  conducted  to  ensure  that  each  request  for 
retroactive approval represents a genuine case given the circumstances.

 Commissioned/Variable Paid employees  

94. Employed individuals (including sales agents) who are paid by commission or a variable 
rate may be approved for a determined tax-free travelling allowance in accordance with 
Section 12 of the ITA and Regulations 8 and 9 of the Second Schedule Part 1 of the Income 
Tax (Employment) Regulations. The procedures stated below should be followed: 

(a)  The employed individuals should fill in the PO1 and Schedule 3 (Employee Expenses 
Claim)  forms  (See  Appendices  6  &  7)  and  take  these  to  any  of  Tax  Administration 
Jamaica  RSCs,  along  with  the  last  Pay  Advice  showing  clearly  the  gross  basic  pay, 
commission  or  variable  pay  received  and  any  travelling  received.  The  Pay  Advice 
should clearly show the year-to-date-figures for all items mentioned. 

(b) At the time of application, the CG will give a determined rate based on the projected 
income of the individual, in addition to the tax- free threshold. This determination will 
be supplied to the employer and employee and the amount is to be applied to the 
income of the employee by the employer before any tax is deducted.  

(c)  At the end of the year the employee is required to submit his/her final return on the 
SO4  form  along  with  all  accompanying  Schedules.  The  employee’s  P24  and  the 
Schedule of Actual Income and Expenditure should accompany this Return. 

This process should be done yearly as the determination made is valid for only one year.  

These forms can be accessed through our web portal at www.jamaicatax.gov.jm .  

 Mandatory On-Line TFTA Applications 

95. Effective January 1, 2021 it became mandatory for employers and or their representatives 
who make applications for TFTA, to make all such applications on-line via their eServices 
accounts on TAJ’s Tax Portal.   

96. All the motor vehicle information, Driver’s Licence information and the Form A and Form 
B  declarations  (when  necessary)  must  be  uploaded  when  submitting  the  application. 
Therefore, effective January 1, 2021 all documentation in relation to the application for 
approval of TFTA must be uploaded in RAIS. Any other critical information which might be 
required, depending on the circumstances of each case must also be uploaded.
